opening_message:
Ticket 1: Diana Cooper (employee ID E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E020.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Diana Cooper (E020) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns the Source Code system, admin is permitted under policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB record for E020 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have at most read (write requires advanced training, admin never permitted). Admin requested exceeds maximum, so grant read.
reason: Diana Cooper (E020) requested admin access to Source Code. The notes conflict: HR states full-time Engineer (which would permit admin since Engineer owns Source Code), but Security DB records her as a contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors may have at most read (write requires advanced training; admin is never permitted for contractors). Given the conflicting employment-type evidence, I apply the more restrictive classification to avoid granting admin in violation of policy, and grant the maximum allowed: read.
